Week in brief

Cross-tenant Edge MAM now protects partner devices as WSL compliance guidance sharpens

The clearest product change is an opt-in Microsoft Edge for Business update supporting cross-tenant Intune Mobile Application Management policies. Most of the remaining material is ordinary compliance documentation restructuring: the central policy-creation guidance now points to platform-specific reference pages and reorganized reporting and noncompliance-action content. The meaningful operational exceptions are new guidance for EPM, WSL compliance, compliance-report interpretation, and Enterprise App Catalog administration.

  • Intune · App management
    Edge for Business adds opt-in cross-tenant Intune MAM support

    A Microsoft 365 Message Center major update says Microsoft Edge for Business now supports cross-tenant Intune Mobile Application Management policies. The opt-in capability can enforce app protection, redirect downloads to OneDrive, and activate leak controls on devices managed by another tenant, directly addressing contractor and partner scenarios. The supplied evidence does not label this as preview or general availability.

  • Endpoint Privilege Management · Device security
    EPM documents an audit-first administrator-to-standard-user migration

    The new Endpoint Privilege Management security guidance recommends auditing first to identify the elevation processes users need. Its audit policy values are Endpoint Privilege Management: Enabled, Default elevation response: Not Configured, Send elevation data for reporting: Yes, and Reporting scope: Diagnostic data and all endpoint elevations. Reporting data can take 24 hours to return, and the guidance suggests observing usage for several weeks when necessary. This is migration guidance, not evidence of a new E​

  • Intune · Device security
    WSL compliance requires a plugin, management extension, and policy cleanup

    The new Windows Subsystem for Linux compliance procedure requires the Intune WSL plugin and the Microsoft Intune management extension. The extension can be installed through an assigned PowerShell script or proactive remediation, a Win32 or Microsoft Store app, or a custom compliance policy. Administrators are also told to unassign and remove existing custom WSL compliance policies and deploy the plugin as a Win32 app. WSL results are incorporated into the host device’s overall compliance state; the page is setup​

  • Intune · Device security
    Compliance reports now spell out check-in lag and multi-user records

    An updated monitoring article clarifies that compliance is evaluated continuously, while reports refresh when a device checks in and show the last confirmed state. Recent assignments may not appear until check-in; devices can remain Pending; shared or multi-user devices may show the previous user’s state; user and system contexts can create multiple records; and summary and detailed views may update at different times. This is a documentation clarification, not an announced change to compliance evaluation behavior.

  • Enterprise App Management · App management
    Enterprise App Catalog guidance sets update targets and Autopilot support

    The new Enterprise App Management procedure states that catalog apps use Microsoft-configured and confirmed default installation, requirements, and detection settings. Most updates are expected to become available within 24 hours after automated validation, while updates requiring manual testing typically take up to seven days. It also documents support for using catalog apps as blocking apps in Windows Autopilot Enrollment Status Page and Device Preparation Page profiles. This is administrative guidance, not a new

For Intune administrators

Evaluate the Edge cross-tenant MAM scenario for contractors and partners, and test app protection, OneDrive download redirection, and leak controls before enabling it. For EPM, use the documented audit-first approach and allow at least 24 hours for reporting data, with longer observation periods where representative usage data is needed. Satisfy the WSL plugin and management-extension prerequisites before deployment. Update compliance-report runbooks to account for check-in lag, pending states, user-context records, and temporary differences between summary and detailed views. Do not infer a product behavior change or feature launch from the broader documentation reorganization.

This period briefing was generated by AI from the tracked Microsoft Learn and Message Center changes.

Microsoft Edge for Business: Cross-tenant support using Intune Mobile Application Management (MAM)

New

Microsoft Edge for Business now supports cross-tenant Intune Mobile Application Management (MAM) policies, enabling data protection on devices managed by different tenants. This opt-in feature enforces app protection, redirects downloads to OneDrive, and activates leak controls, enhancing security for contractors and partners without disrupting users.
